content:
Apple's YouTube channel shared a video today showcasing the new and old features of Apple "Family" accounts that parents can manage. You can watch it below.

"Scrolling the phone and other things"

A few days ago, we reported that Apple, with the launch of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27, added many new features to the parental controls suite across its devices.

Today Apple released a fun new animated video introducing some of those new features, while also mentioning existing features, to help parents make "kids safer on iPhone, iPad, and Mac," as Apple puts it.

Apple explains it all starts with setting up a Family account, which then lets parents choose age-appropriate protections for their own devices.

Once set up, Apple walks through how parents can control what types of apps their kids can access, approve new apps and games through Ask to Buy, and use the new Ask to Browse feature to approve or deny Safari website access.

The video also highlights controls for approving new contacts, expanded Communication Safety features, new Time Allowances and Schedules features, and more.

Worth noting is that, although the art style is quite different, this video has slight echoes of the "Intention" video Apple showed at the opening of WWDC 2013 — both use simple graphics and playful motion to convey the meaning and feeling they're going for.
